newsitem.title: UK: BoE move biggest economic decision since war - Blair.
newsitem.headline: BoE move biggest economic decision since war - Blair.

text.p: Tony Blair believes the new Labour government's handover of responsibility for setting interest rates to the Bank of England is the biggest step in economic policy-making in Britain since World War Two, an aide to the Prime Minister said on Tuesday.
He quoted Blair as describing the decision as a bold, decisive act of leadership that showed Labour was intent on hitting the ground running and redeeming its core election manifesto commitments.
"It shows we will shrink from no decision that helps the long-term prosperity of Britain and its people," the aide said.

Blair will underline his determination to govern as "New Labour" in a start-of-term speech to his parliamentary party on Wednesday, telling all 419 members of parliament that their large majority gave Labour an added responsibility to govern in the same disciplined way as it ran for office.
Blair, learning from the mistakes of past Labour administrations, is keen to ensure that the parliamentary party is a source of support for, not opposition to, the government, aides said.
He also wants to keep up the careful coordination of policy formulation and enunciation that was Labour's hallmark in the run-up to the election.
Peter Mandelson, a close Blair confidante who masterminded Labour's election campaign, will chair a meeting every morning aimed at getting across the government's message as policy unfolds.
The meeting will be attended by members of the private office of Blair, deputy Prime Minister John Prescott and Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown.
Blair's press secretary, Alistair Campbell, his deputy and Government Chief Whip Nick Brown will also take part.
Aides played down reports in some newspapers on Tuesday that the new prime minister was running a presidential regime.
But in another sign that Blair intends to keep a tight grip on the government machine, requests for major interviews with ministers will have to be cleared in advance with Campbell.
Blair celebrated his 44th birthday on Tuesday by inviting 10 Downing Street staff to the cabinet room to share three birthday cakes that he had been given.
